transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-22
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 38 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rajiv Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Morales (Silverpine Head of ML), Dr. Samir Chawla (Clinical Lead), Jordan White (Product)
Links referenced: pilot results sheet (https://docs.silverpine.health/pilot-results), security pack (link shared in chat), Redwood bisect report (will be shared)

Summary:
Quick triage of quality regressions spotted in last week's run. Focus on prompt-bisection to isolate failure modes, check guardrail rule interactions, and plan a Dedicated capacity perf run. Decided Redwood will run bisect tests and return artifacts; Silverpine to annotate edge cases.

Topics:
- Which prompt sets regressed and how many examples fail
- Scoring thresholds and mismatch between automatic score and human pass/fail
- Guardrail false positives on clinical phrasing
- Next steps and ownership

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for hopping on. We wanted to run through the regression list you sent and do a quick bisect plan. Is that still the right agenda?
[00:12] Elena (Silverpine): Yes thanks, Maya. We had about 4 prompt sets spike in failure yesterday — mainly the med-summary and intake-triage flows. Some are subtle, like swapped meds, and some are hallucinations.
[00:25] Rajiv (Redwood SE): Got it. I pulled the run logs — there's a cluster of lower-likelihood tokens in those outputs and some guardrail triggers that might be interfering. I suspect a prompt-template change plus a model variant shift.
[00:40] Jordan (Product): I just want to call out business impact — we saw a 12% drop in pass-rate on triage which triggered manual reviews, so it's definitely urgent.
[00:55] Samir (Clinical): For clinical safety, a single hallucinated dose is a blocker. We need high precision on medication extraction.
[01:10] Maya: Understood. Rajiv, can you explain the bisect approach you propose?
[01:20] Rajiv: Sure. We'll run a progressive bisect: first baseline the model family (open-model-7B vs optimized-7B-q), then isolate prompt-template diffs, then the guardrail set toggles. We'll instrument token-level log probs and the k v cash — sorry K V cache — metrics so we can see where the model goes off.
[01:40] Elena: When you say model family, I thought we pinned to the redwood-verified-7b. We did pin that but the hosted env fell back to a smaller shard overnight then it rolled back — maybe that caused drift.
[01:55] Maya: Yeah sometimes routing falls back to a variant under high load, we can check smart routing logs. That's a good hypothesis.
[02:10] Rajiv: Also important — our scoring threshold is 0.65 but human raters are disagreeing until 0.8 on some intents. We should reconcile that.
[02:25] Elena: We have an evaluation doc where human labels are 'pass/needs-review/fail' — maybe we should map that to numeric tiers. I'll share mapping.
[02:36] Jordan: Quick question on guardrails: we were seeing false positives when clinicians used shorthand like 'qpm' and the guardrail flagged it as PII. Is there a way to tune that without opening new holes?
[02:50] Rajiv: Yes, the guardrail engine supports exception rules and context-aware patterns, but you have to be careful. We'll try a targeted rule relax for common clinical abbreviations and run a false-positive sweep.
[03:05] Samir: Please annotate examples — we can send 20-30 annotated samples from yesterday's failures.
[03:15] Elena: We'll do that.
[03:20] Maya: Great. For the bisect, we'll do these steps: 1) run model-variant compare on the failing prompt set, 2) run prompt-template diff bisection (e.g. remove chunks to find the breaking token), 3) toggle guardrail subsets. We'll put results in the sheet.
[03:36] Rajiv: One thing to watch — when we run on Dedicated, batching and KV caching behave differently than hosted; performance artifacts can affect beam-search-ish outputs. So the Dedicated perf run planned for next week will also be an opportunity to see if the failure is infra-related.
[03:55] Elena: Do you mean Redwood Dedicated or our private deployment?
[04:00] Rajiv: Redwood Dedicated — reserved capacity in our cloud. We can also replicate in your VPC if you want but that requires more setup.
[04:10] Jordan: For now Dedicated is fine, it's faster to instrument.
[04:18] Maya: Action items — we'll run bisect and share logs + highlight top 10 diffs. Also we'll run the guardrail false-positive sweep.
[04:30] Elena: We'll upload annotated examples and clarifications about label mapping.
[04:36] Samir: On the clinical side, we want to know any changes that could impact dosing or allergy extraction specifically.
[04:45] Rajiv: We'll add an explicit check for med/dose/allergy spans and include a small unit test for that in the eval harness.
[04:55] Speaker 1: (inaudible) yeah but also, the scorer — is it still using renormalized log-probs or a separate reranker?
[05:05] Rajiv: It's a mix — primary score is model confidence with a downstream reranker for high-value intents. We can run a reranker-only pass to see if that recovers some examples.
[05:20] Elena: If reranker recovers, that suggests model output is salvageable with post-processing, which might be less risky than changing prompts.
[05:30] Maya: Good point. We'll include a reranker pass in the bisect matrix.
[05:38] Rajiv: Timeline — bisect run today/tonight, initial results in 24-48 hours, full report by Friday. That align with your release?
[05:48] Elena: Yes, we're aiming to freeze prompt changes Monday, so earlier is better.
[05:55] Jordan: Also, can Redwood share a short note on any infra changes on your side last week that might have triggered fallback routing? Even a summary is helpful for our audit.
[06:05] Maya: Yep we'll share the routing events and any config changes. Also we'll include the smart routing decision logs.
[06:15] Samir: On compliance: we need confirmation that logs will not include PHI in cleartext in the shared sheets. How does Redwood mask tokens in logs?
[06:28] Rajiv: We mask sensitive spans and provide hashed identifiers; for the bisect we'll provide masked logs but still allow you to map back with your keys if you want deeper debugging. We'll attach our security pack (SOC2 section + KMS guidance) to the CR.
[06:42] Elena: Perfect, please send that.
[06:48] Maya: Ok to recap — Redwood bisect + reranker pass (Maya/Rajiv), share results link by 2025-07-23, Dedicated perf run scheduled 2025-07-29, Silverpine to upload annotations by 2025-07-24. Any other items?
[07:05] Jordan: Can we also get a short doc on how to interpret token-prob dumps? The engineers here will want to read it.
[07:12] Rajiv: We'll include a short readme in the sheet.
[07:18] Elena: Thanks all.
[07:20] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links and the bisect plan.

End of transcript.

Recap / Explicit next steps (aligned with metadata):
- Redwood: run prompt bisection, reranker-only pass, guardrail false-positive sweep; share bisect report and smart-routing logs (due 2025-07-23).
- Silverpine: upload annotated edge cases and label mapping (due 2025-07-24).
- Joint: Dedicated perf+eval run on 2025-07-29.

Notes on quality and quirks:
- Transcription contains occasional mis-hearings ("K V cash" for KV cache, speaker attribution for one short section).
- Several technical terms and product names may be slightly off in transcript (e.g., redwood-verified-7b typed as redwood-verified-7 b).
